chapter: Brawls, the Ink Spots and boyhood recollections
title: Indianapolis theatres and the first Ink Spots trio
summary: He won a bicycle contest, played the big Indianapolis theatres, and added Sugar Babe to make a trio billed as the Ink Spots.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So anyway, I quieted him down on the idea of us boxing or anybody fighting in this group, after they saw me fight, they saw I was too good for this boy. So I got my papers daily with all impunity, nobody said anything against my getting them or nothing. So we all got along fine. Then I went to get into this Indianapolis contest to win a bicycle, you know, the first prize is a bicycle and so forth and I get that all right.

And then I played all the biggest theaters in Indianapolis from the New Royal, which is the biggest theater, and we got to Indianapolis, you know, I got a trio together. See it was only Buck and Bubbles at the time and then I got a little boy called Sugar Babe and we put him in the act and made a trio and we were the first Ink Spots, you

know. Buck and Bubbles and Sugar Babe were the first Ink Spots out of Indianapolis, Indiana, where Deek Watson who is one of the Ink Spots now, took the name and started the Ink Spots with Bill Kenny 'cause he's from Indianapolis -- Deek.

However, the Lyric Theater in Indianapolis is where we did the act called the three Ink Spots. It was sensational. We played in the Royal Theater which is the biggest theater in Indianapolis and I played the Two Johns and I played the Senate Theater and played every theater they had that was more or less worth our playing.
And I also worked in the five and ten cents store, J.J. McCrory, I think it is. I was a janitor in the five and ten cents store.
Can you describe a little bit about who the Ink Spots were and what they became?
